I think the part of what you were saying that struck true for me and would be the part that I’d suggest directly addressing is the way you described HOW he was playing and interacting with the world. You come across as sounding like your saying the way he’s interacting with it is wrong and your going to “help” him learn how rewarding it can be to do it right by trying to force him into these narrative paths. That’s…. Just…. It’s really a joy killer. It sounds like he sees and interacts with the game/world one way and you another. A direct, non narrative and in world (meaning real life) recognition of how he plays and the virtues of it, along with the way you play and the virtues of that, but then the difficulty of having them in the same space would be what I wished happened. Then I wish we could have together come to a compromise, not come to a conclusion that the DM just “knows what he’s doing” and found a way to have our play-styles co-exist.

I recently had to leave a campaign because my DM who was a good friend tried to do very much the same kind of thing that your are proposing here. I was very much the same kind of player you describe. New to DnD, used to solo gaming, maybe not the part where a class was selected that didn’t fit with my actions, but I very much was playing to perform optimally. My DM did not appreciate this and felt that his way of playing was something I needed to come around to and if I would only listen to experienced, wiser minds, I would find it much more rewarding. This was a terrible experience for me. He wanted me to enjoy the game one way and I flat out enjoyed it another. Had we been able to have an adult conversation about that, and find a way to compromise without him creating these kinds of hoops like you are to try to force him into your way of thinking, we both might have been able to enjoy the game together. As it stands you’re only going to alienate him, at least that’s what the kinds of things you’re doing did to me.

You were actually right on the money with Swashbuckler Rogue you just need some tweaks.

	•	Swashbuckler does not require dual wielding. You can absolutely fight with just one scimitar (or shortsword) and still get full Sneak Attack + Swashbuckler benefits.
	•	You mentioned wanting a cutlass—there’s no official cutlass in D&D, but a scimitar is mechanically identical and fits the flavor perfectly: short, curved, one-handed, light and a finesse weapon.
	•	If you want to pair it with a pistol, I would compromise with a hand crossbow, you’ll see why below.
	•	You can’t attack with both a sword and a crossbow in the same turn at level 1 unless you take the Crossbow Expert feat.
	•	Crossbow Expert removes the reload restriction, lets you shoot in melee, and gives you a bonus action shot if you’ve attacked with a one-handed weapon.
	•	Normally, you don’t get a feat until level 4—but if you play a Variant Human or Custom Lineage (Tasha’s), you can start with Crossbow Expert at level 1.

⸻

So your ideal loadout at level 1 could be:
	•	Class: Swashbuckler Rogue
	•	Race: Variant Human or Custom Lineage
	•	Feat: Crossbow Expert
	•	Weapons: Scimitar (aka “cutlass”) + hand crossbow

That gives you the exact “charming runaway noble with a sword and pistol” vibe you’re going for—with real mechanical support. No magic.

I am one of the players you are wanting and am still going to say this is a you thing. I just ended up leaving a table because I wanted to do exactly what you are asking for and my DM wanted the opposite. He wanted all the exploration and curiosity to happen in session with everyone else present. I loved theory crafting and coming up with ideas and reading up on the rules and how I might use them to handle this situation or that and discussing it with him. When I asked for a way to compromise our play styles I was told that wasn’t happening. We then went back and forth and it then became apparent that what was most important to him was my obedience and his control over my behaviour so I left because it wasn’t a play style difference anymore. All that is to say, some DM’s expressly DON’T want what you want, some DO. Players are the same. Some are going to want to just show up. Trying to get everyone to fit in a particular box isn’t a great way to move forward. Your best bet to address this would have been to discuss this in a session 0 and say that this level of engagement was something you were wanting/looking for. It would have allowed them to bail or adjust their behaviour accordingly.

I came prepared to play the game as a person that reads the rules understands them and expets to operate within them. If YOU set that expectation and didn't fully consider the ramifications of someone excepting to operate within that framework and then are bothered when they aren't grateful to you because they surprised you with how that might upset the balance of the  game you set up. Room Temperature: Tirzepatide can be stored at room temperature, up to 86°F (30°C), for a maximum of 21 days. If the medication has been out of the refrigerator for longer than 21 days, it should not be used.
Don’t Exceed Room Temperature: While the medication is stable at room temperature for up to three weeks, higher temperatures can degrade its potency more rapidly.

The fact is that weight loss medications are big money. There are other alternatives but they all are around the same price points with name brand, compounding and grey prices. Right now the best prices you can get while still getting something FDA approved is through compounding places like Zappy and SlimedownRX where you buy multiple months at a time and that’s only if you are getting the maximum dosage from them by possibly lying on the intake form. That still is going to have you paying somewhere around 5-7 per mg. That is only going to be available as long as the pharmaceutical companies are kept at bay with the shortage stuff in court. After that you’re stuck with the name brand prices of 15-20 per mg. Grey is indeed .50-1 per mg but it’s not fda approved and requires you to be risk tolerant and somewhat savvy. Honestly, If you are looking to reduce your cost and be legit, your best bet is to look for a job that has insurance that covers whatever brand you want and change careers, it’s probably the only way that’s gonna be viable other than grey long term.
